θερίτροπος.definition: turning in summer, of the solstice, Tz.ad Hes.Op.596

θαύμακτρον.definition: money paid to see conjurers' tricks, Sophr.120

θεόσυτος.definition: sent by the gods, A.Pr.116; ib.596 :—also ib.643

θεοκρήπις.definition: founded by a god, of Athens, Nonn.D.24.96

θητεῖον.definition: = title of play by Sopatros, Ath.4.175c, al

θεραπήϊος.definition: Ion. and poet. for in neut. pl. AP7.158.8:— fem. Orac. ap. Jul.Ep.88b

θυμίασις.definition: fumigating, Dsc.1.98, Antyll. ap; passing off in fumes, Arist.Mete.387a30; Porph.Abst.2.5

θυμβροφάγος.definition: eating savory, to look as if one had eaten savory, 'make a verjuice face', Ar.Ach.254

θρύον.definition: reed, rush, Il.21.351, Hp.Steril.246; = thornapple, Datura Stramonium, Orph.A.916, Thphr.HP9.11.6 , Dsc.4.73

θραύπαλος.definition: joint fir, Ephedra campulopoda, Thphr.HP3.6.4; ib.4.1.3

θύϊνος.definition: of the tree , Str.4.6.2, v.l. in Dsc.1.22; made of this wood, Callix.1, Apoc.18.12

θεόκριτος.definition: judge of gods, of Paris, Dosiad.Ara10

θηριομάχης.definition: one who fights with beasts, D.S.36.10

θεοφίλιον.definition: eyesalve invented by Theophilus, Aët.7.115, Alex.Trall.2

θερειλεχής.definition: for sleeping under in summer, Nic.Th.584

θυραῖος.definition: absent, abroad, A.Ag.1608, Ch.115; to come from abroad, E.Ion702 ; in the public eye, opp. Id.Med.217

θωρακεῖον.definition: = II, breastwork, parapet, or; gunwale of a trireme, IG22.1604.31

θερμοχύτης.definition: vessel for hot drinks, AP9.587 tit

θεαγωγέω.definition: evoke gods, Iamb.Myst.3.6:—hence ib.2.10:— Adj. PMag.Par.1.975,985

θύννειος.definition: of the tunny-fish, pickled; tunny-fishery, IG4.752.7

θηροφανής.definition: appearing like a beast, Procl.ad Hes.Op.151

θαέομαι.definition: Dor. for , Pi.P.8.45: aor. 1 Lyr.Adesp.40; imper. Epigr. ap. Phan.Hist.12; cf

θιγάνα.definition: cover, lid, dub. in Schwyzer323 C39

θνητόψυχος.definition: maintaining the mortality of the soul, Tz.H.8.222

θηλυμίτρης.definition: with a woman's in woman's clothes, Luc.DDeor.18.1: acc. prob. cj. for Id.Bacch.3

θηρευτής.definition: hunter, used by Hom; metaph., Pl.Sph.231d, cf. Chor.p.67 B.; Ath.3.122c

θηλύτης.definition: womanhood, female nature; womanishness, delicacy, Corn.ND20, Plu.Crass.32; the womanish nature of . . , ib.24; also, effeminacy, Id.Alc.16

θάκησις.definition: means of sitting, seat, prob. in S.OC9

θηριοτρόφος.definition: abounding in wild beasts, of; proparox., Pass., fed on reptiles, Gal.11.143

θεόπεμπτος.definition: sent by the gods, Arist.EN1099b15; superhuman, extraordinary, Longus3.18

θεοδοσία.definition: a gift or offering to the gods, Str.17.1.37

θωΰσσω.definition: of a dog, bark, bay, Hom.Fr.25; of a gnat; c. acc. pers., call on, call, . . Id.OC1624: c. dat., shout to dogs, E.Hipp.219 , cf.Ba.871

θρασύμαχος.definition: bold in battle, Arist.Rh.1400b20: as pr. n., Thrasymachus:—hence Adj. style of T., D.H.Dem.3

θυμελαία.definition: prob. spurge-flax, Daphne Cnidium, Dsc.4.172, Plin. HN13.114:—hence wine flavoured with Dsc.5.68

θλάσπις.definition: Ion. shepherd's purse, Capsella bursapastoris, Hp.Mul.1.78, al.:—also Dsc.2.156, Plin.HN 27.140:—Dim. Ps.-Dsc.2.156

θεοφόρητος.definition: possessed by a god, inspired; Act., carrying a god or goddess, Luc.Asin.37

θεοδώρητος.definition: given by God, Iamb.VP2.6, 15.67; of the Zos.Alch.p.114B

θηριώνυμος.definition: named after a wild beast, Eust.ad D.P.976

θεότρεπτος.definition: turned by the gods, these divine changes of fortune, A.Pers.905

θρίγκωμα.definition: coping, cornice, cj. for J.AJ15.11.3: metaph., of salt, Plu.2.685b

θερμάζω.definition: = sq., Ep. aor. 1 opt. Med. Nic.Al.587

θεμιστεῖος.definition: of law and right, the sceptre of righteous judgement, Pi.O.1.12

θαῦμα.definition: of objects, wonder, marvel, in Ep. always in sg., Il.13.99, etc.; of Polyphemus, Od.9.190; of a beautiful woman, 11.287; of Hercules, S.Tr.961 , etc.: freq. c. inf., a wonder to behold, Il.5.725, etc.; h.Ven.205, Hes.…

θεομοιρία.definition: the god's portion of a sacrifice, SIG1026.20

θηρόβοτος.definition: where wild beasts feed, AP9.4 , cf. Phalar.Ep.34

θυανία.definition: prob. f.l. for Dor. for Epich.148

θεράπνη.definition: poet., = handmaid; as pr. n. a Laconian city, Pi.P.11.63, Hdt.6.61, etc.; Lacon. Alcm.4: in pl. Isoc.10.63

θεομανία.definition: madness caused by God, inspiration, cj. in Ph.1.571

θρύμμα.definition: that which is broken off, bit, Hp.Mul.1.75, Ar.Fr.160, Aglaïas20, Gal.6.343; AP6.232

θανάσιμος.definition: belonging to death, the life-blood, A.Ag.1019 ; having sung her death-song, ib.1445; E.Hipp.1438

θηλυχίτων.definition: with woman's frock, AP6.219 , Orac. ap. Luc.Alex.27

θηκαῖος.definition: like a chest or coffin; Subst. = SIG1120

θωρακοπώλης.definition: dealer in breastplates, Ar.Pax in Ind. personarum

θανατόω.definition: fut. A.Pr.1053 , etc.: pf; Pass., of flesh, to be mortified, Hp.Fract.26:—metaph. in Act., mortify, Ep.Rom.8.13

θεόκλυτος.definition: calling on the gods, A.Th.143; Pass., heard by God, expl. of Ishmael, J.AJ1.10.4

θυρσεχθής.definition: of Bacchus, prob. f.l. for with thyrsus-spear, Orph.H.45.5

θρυαλλίς.definition: plantain, Plantago crassifolia; wick, Ar.Ach.874,al., Philyll.26

θαμβόομαι.definition: to be terrified, pf. part. Aët.16.66

θηροκόμος.definition: keeping wild beasts or camels, Hld.10.27

θεουργία.definition: divine work, Jul.Or.7.219a; sacramental rite, 'mystery', Porph. ap. Aug.Civ.D.10.9; Iamb.Myst.9.6; Procl.in Alc.p.92C

θεόπνοος.definition: contr. = foreg., Corp.Herm.1.30; Numen. ap. Porph.Antr.10; of the Sphinx, Epigr.Gr.1016

θυμοξάλμη.definition: drink of thyme, vinegar, and brine, Dsc.5.16

θηριονάρκη.definition: a plant that benumbs serpents, Nerium Oleander, Plin.HN24.163,25.113

θερμοδότης.definition: one who brought the hot water at baths, Gloss.:—fem. female bath-attendant, AP9.183

θεόχρηστος.definition: delivered by God, of the Mosaic Law, Ph.2.577

θυραυλία.definition: living out of doors, camping out; waiting at the door, of lovers, in pl., Ph.1.155, Philostr.Ep.29: sg., Luc.Merc.Cond.10

θέμις.definition: old Ep. gen. (in Hom. the only; that which is laid down or established, law as established by custom, 'tis meet and right, c. dat. pers. et inf., Od.14.56; Il.11.779; Hes.Sc.22; SIG1024.9 : without dat., Il.16.796, 23…

θεράπευμα.definition: a service done to another; divine worship, Pl.Def.415a

θεοπλάστης.definition: maker of gods, i.e. of their; the divine Creator, Ph.2.490

θεόφοιτος.definition: driven by divine frenzy, of Cassandra, Tryph.374

θινίον.definition: Dim. of I.2, dub. in Phld.D.3.7; coined as etym. of AB367

θειασμός.definition: superstition; inspiration, frenzy, D.H.7.68; such as D.T.642.17

θεοκατάρατος.definition: accursed of God, Zos.Alch. ap. Olymp.Alch.p.101 B

θήραρχος.definition: commander of two elephants, Ascl.Tact.9, Ael.Tact.23:—hence his command, Ascl.Tact.9

θεσπέσιος.definition: also E.Andr.296; divinely uttered or decreed, dat. sg. fem. as Adv., Il.2.367

θρεπτήριος.definition: feeding, nourishing, A.Ch.545; hair dedicated as a thank- offering to Inachus, ib.6

θεσπιῳδέω.definition: to be a sing in prophetic; hold office of i. e. versifier of oracles, OGI530.6 , IGRom.4.1588 , etc

θεοφορία.definition: = Phld.Mus.p.25K., Iamb.Myst.3.5,al.: pl., Phld.Mus.p.49K., Str.12.3.32, 16.2.36:—sg. in poet. form AP6.220.4

θηροτρόφος.definition: feeding wild beasts, IGRom.4.826; proparox., Pass., feeding on beasts, E.Ph.820

θλῖψις.definition: pressure, Arist.Mete.382a13, Pr.890a2; crushing, castration, Hippiatr.20

θεόγλωσσος.definition: with the tongue of a god, of poetesses, AP9.26

θροέω.definition: aor. poet. B.3.9, S.Aj.947; c. acc., tell out, utter aloud, Id.Ag.1137 ; ib.1141 , cf. 104; S.OC597; ib.1425.—Rare. exc. in Trag.; in late Prose, J.AJ18.6.10, 19.1.16

θρέψις.definition: nourishing, S.E.M.11.97, cf. Alex.Aphr.Pr.2.66, Gal.1.655, etc

θρανίτης.definition: rower on the topmost; Adj. of the topmost bench, the topmost bench, Plb.16.3.4:- fem. the oar of a IG22.1604.52 , EM454.12

θυρσοφορέω.definition: bear the thyrsus, D.S.4.3; assemble or lead companies with the thyrsus, E.Ba.557

θήρευσις.definition: hunting, the chase, ib.824a: metaph., Id.Tht.166c

θεογονία.definition: Ion. genealogy of the gods; generation or birth of gods, Pl.Lg.886c, Ph.2.205, 264, D.L.Praef.3

θηγανίτης.definition: a hard stone, used for whetstones, gen. IG14.317

θέορτος.definition: sprung from the gods, Pi.O.2.36; A.Pr.765

θεοτόκος.definition: mother of God, of the Virgin, Cod.Just.1.1.5.1, Just.Nov.3.1, SIG910B

θυλακίτης.definition: = sq., only fem. the common poppy , Dsc.4.64; = Id.1.9

θειότης.definition: divine nature, divinity; f.l.for Isoc.11.26, Plu.2.857a, and so prob. in Id.Sull.6

θηρολετέω.definition: destroy wild beasts, Eust.561.3, Dosith.p.432 K

θύραθεν.definition: Adv.from outside the door: and generally; outside the door, outside, E.Fr.1063.4; Arist.Resp.480a30, cf. PA642b1, foreigners, the enemy, A.Th.68, 193

θρασύνω.definition: = embolden, encourage; c. acc., boast of, Plb.4.31.4

θερμοκύαμος.definition: a leguminous plant, of a kind between the and the Diph.87

θεοφιλότης.definition: a being loved by God, Men.Rh.pp.361,362 S

θυρεαμαχία.definition: contest in which shields were borne, SIG1061.12

θησαυρίζω.definition: store, treasure up; abs., hoard, lay up treasure, Phld.Oec.p.71J., Ep.Jac.5.3; Ev.Luc.12.21

θυηπολέω.definition: trans., sacrifice, S.Fr.126, cf. 522, Maiist.13:—Pass., is filled with sacrifices by them, E.Heracl.401

θαλαμεύω.definition: lead into the i.e. take to wife, Hld.4.6:—Pass., of women, to be shut up, kept at home, Aristaenet.2.5; to be taken to wife, Ph.1.323

θερμολούτης.definition: one who uses hot baths, Agathin. ap. Orib.10.7.9

θεσπιδαής.definition: kindled by a god, portentous fire, Il.12.177, 441, Od.4.418, etc

θηλύτροπος.definition: of womanish habit: metaph., of the planet Venus, Cat.Cod.Astr.1.136

θρόνον.definition: only in pl. flowers embroidered on; herbs used as drugs and charms, Theoc.2.59, Nic.Th.493,936, Lyc.674, Aglaïas7; used in sacrificial offering, UPZ96.4

θέαινα.definition: Ep. for goddess, in Hom. mostly in phrase Il.8.5, cf. Od.8.341, al.; Antiph.81.3: in later Ep., Call.Dian.29

θέλησις.definition: a willing, will, Stoic.3.41; goodwill, favour, LXXPr.8.35

θεομαντεῖον.definition: spell for evoking a divine revelation, PMag.Leid.V.5.13

θολομιγής.definition: mixed with dirt, Onat. ap. Stob.1.1.39

θόωσα.definition: speedy, swift, as pr. n. Od.1.71, Emp.122.3

θεόρακτος.definition: struck, i.e. maddened, by God, nickname of Cic. Verr.4.66.148

θεόμοιρος.definition: partaking of the divine nature, Ecphant. ap. Stob.4.6.22; Dam.Isid.191

θρόμβος.definition: lump, Hdt.1.179; clot of; drop, . . Ev.Luc.22.44

θυροειδής.definition: like a door, dub. in Hippiatr.40 ; the opening in the os pubis, Gal.2.414

θυροκοπέω.definition: knock at the door, break it open, esp. as; metaph., knock as at a door, Plu.2.503a; Alciphr.3.70

θυρεοφορέω.definition: to be armed with the oblong shield, Plb.10.13.2

θάλαμος.definition: an inner room or chamber, surrounded; generally, women's apartment, inner part of the house, like Il.3.142,174, Od.4.121, etc.: in pl., Il.18.492; . . Hdt.1.34

θυροκόπος.definition: knocking at the door, begging, A.Ag.1195

θηλύσπορος.definition: of female kind, of the daughters of Danaus, A.Pr.855

θεοτέρατος.definition: with divine portents, of Io's wanderings, dithyrambic phrase in Demetr.Eloc.91 codd

θυείδιον.definition: Dim. of Ar.Pl.710; wrongly written in cod. Rav., as in Damocr. ap. Gal.14.118

θυμόμαντις.definition: prophesying from one's own soul, A.Pers.224 ; cf

θεματισμός.definition: laying down: hence; conventional arrangement, Vitr.1.2.5

θαλασσίτης.definition: wine sunk in the sea, to ripen it, Plin.HN14.78

θύννα.definition: female tunny, f.l. in Hippon.35.2: Antiph.129.4, Archestr.Fr.37.1

θηρόβορος.definition: eaten or torn by wild beasts, Ps.Phoc.147; death by wild beasts, Man.4.614

θερμοπλάω.definition: have inflammation in the hoof, of horses, Hippiatr.53

θεόφαντος.definition: revealed by God or revealing God, Metrod. 38

θέσκελος.definition: Ep. Adj. perh. set in motion by God , and so marvellous, wondrous, always of things, deeds or works of wonder, Il.3.130, Od.11.610; Call.Fr.anon.385: neut. Adv., it was wondrous like him, Il.23.107; prob. taken by lat…

θρᾶνος.definition: bench, form, Ar.Pl.545 (gen; close-stool, Hp. ap. Gal.19.104

θηριάζομαι.definition: Pass., pass into a beast, of the soul, Corp.Herm.10.20

θηρομιγής.definition: half-beast, of centaurs, Opp.C.2.6; a cry as of beasts, Plu.Mar.20

θεότης.definition: divinity, divine nature, Ep.Col.2.9, Plu.2.359d, Luc.Icar.9, etc.; for religious reasons, Heliod. ap. Orib.50.7.1

θεοτερπής.definition: of a dish, fit for the gods, Philox.2.9; pleasing to God, AP9.197 ; cf

θραῦσις.definition: comminution, opp; slaughter, LXX2 Ki.17.9; destruction by plague, ib.24.15, Nu.16.48

θεόταυρος.definition: god-bull, a name for Zeus, Mosch.2.135
